# Protect one intended effect across repeated attempts

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `messaging-idempotent-consumer` · **Messaging & Event-Driven Systems** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S04-Q024](#S04-Q024)

<p>How would you design an idempotent consumer so repeated at-least-once deliveries do not repeat an intended business effect? Trace your design under a retry and concurrent deliveries.</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Design and verify a consumer that preserves the intended database effect across retries and concurrent deliveries.</p>

<ul>
<li>Define stable operation identity and the business invariant it protects.</li>
<li>Trace uniqueness, business changes and commit/acknowledgment boundaries under concurrency.</li>
<li>Test repetition, partial failure and conflicting identities without assuming every timeout proves failure.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>Inspect how database identity restrictions interact with business changes before designing the full consumer. Then trace repeated and concurrent attempts. The source import scenario combines that effect guarantee with submission behavior, recovery, observability and scaling.</p>

<a id="S04-Q026"></a>

### S04-Q026 · Mechanism

<p>How can a database unique constraint support deduplication when several workers process the same operation? Explain what it protects and what still needs a transaction-level design.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q026](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q026)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q026](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q026)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do database unique constraints help deduplication?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>A unique constraint restricts repeated key values in stored data. Connect that restriction to the business effect instead of assuming that rejecting one insert solves the whole operation.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about database-enforced identity under concurrency.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Assume a relational database and a non-null stable operation key. State the transaction boundary; check product-specific conflict behavior before choosing error handling.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace competing inserts together with the associated business update.</li>
<li>Identify a failure window and a test that would expose an unprotected effect.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Marking an operation handled before ensuring its business update succeeds.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you distinguish a duplicate operation from a different constraint violation?</li>
<li>What happens if the operation marker and business update use different databases?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q024"></a>

### S04-Q024 · Application

<a id="S04-Q025"></a>

<p>How would you design an idempotent consumer so repeated at-least-once deliveries do not repeat an intended business effect? Trace your design under a retry and concurrent deliveries.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q024](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q024) · [S04-Q025](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q025)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q024](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q024)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do you prevent duplicate processing when delivery is at-least-once?

</div>

**[S04-Q025](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q025)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do you design an idempotent consumer?

</div>

**Why these source prompts share a canonical question:** Same duplicate-effect/idempotent-consumer contract under repeated delivery.

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Idempotent means repetition preserves the intended outcome. The question concerns duplicate effects, not a promise that the broker performs only one delivery.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Protect a business invariant across repeated and concurrent processing attempts.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify stable operation identity, the local transaction boundary and any external effects. Provider-specific delivery guarantees require separate verification.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explain the relationship between identifying an operation and committing its effect.</li>
<li>Test interruption after commit and simultaneous attempts, stating the guarantee boundary.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Relying on a process-local check to coordinate all worker replicas.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What if the same operation ID arrives with different business data?</li>
<li>How would deduplication retention affect a later replay?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-SC001"></a>

### S04-SC001 · Production decision

<p>A client repeatedly submits the same large import while its first job is still running. Design the submission and worker flow so that retries are safe and only the intended work is performed.</p>

**Source:** [S04-SC001](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#production-scenario)

<p>This editorial scenario ID identifies an existing unnumbered source scenario. Its steps and constraints are not separate source questions.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-SC001](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#production-scenario)**

Open the source link for the complete original constraints. The scenario remains one source unit; its original Markdown is also preserved in the shared inventory.

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Preserve every source constraint: duplicate messages must not create duplicate database rows; failed messages must be recoverable; processing state must be observable; multiple worker replicas must scale horizontally.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design an inspectable import workflow that protects intended effects under repetition and failure.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify what identifies the same import, concurrent-submission behavior, transaction boundaries and caller-visible state. The source does not prescribe an API, broker or import format.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace repeated submission, concurrent workers and interruption around commit.</li>
<li>Provide a failure matrix showing safe recovery, visible state and horizontal-scale constraints.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Deduplicating only at submission while ignoring duplicate worker deliveries.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What should happen when the same request identity contains different import data?</li>
<li>How would you resume a partially processed import without duplicating rows?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>Two ASP.NET Core worker replicas receive the same account-credit operation. Design the state transitions and test cases for simultaneous delivery, a crash around commit, an acknowledgment loss and the same identity with different credit data. State which database effect is protected and how an external notification changes the boundary.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Identifies a repeated operation and explains the intended single business effect.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Defends the concurrency and transaction boundary, traces ambiguous outcomes and supplies failure tests with explicit limits.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>A happy-path duplicate check without concurrent and interrupted-attempt evidence cannot establish the claimed effect guarantee.</p>
